mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior 3 months reduces the cost of capital, increasing equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5% and remains above this threshold for 3 consecutive months, restrictive monetary policy suppresses equity growth, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate labor market contraction, reducing corporate earnings growth and causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where both UNRATE and PAYEMS decline, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1000 units signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST < 1000 during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction (HOUST) over the prior 3 months indicates strong consumer demand, supporting corporate revenue growth and producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST has increased over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 for 3 consecutive months, manufacturing slowdown reduces corporate output and profits, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100 for 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2% and FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for 3 months signal accelerating inflation and aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where both CPIAUCSL > 2% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.5%), a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 140,000 thousand signals worsening labor market conditions, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS < 140000 during high-unemployment regime, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
